correctness.rationale: For every \(r>0\), \(\ell>0\), \(m=\sin^2\theta\in[0,1)\), support additivity gives width \(2r\sqrt{1-U_3^2}+\ell|\sin\theta\,U_2+\cos\theta\,U_3|\). The conditional absolute cosine integral is analytically evaluated by integration by parts and the standard complete-elliptic integral identity, yielding \(F=2[2\mathbf E(m)-(1-m)\mathbf K(m)]/(3\pi)\). The exact derivative \(\frac{dF}{dm}=(3\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^2\phi/\sqrt{1-m\sin^2\phi}\,d\phi\) is positive with sharp endpoint limits \(1/12\) and \(1/(3\pi)\), proving every finite-parameter variance and inverse assertion. The supplied checker separately re-integrates original spherical conditional formulas and tests Cartesian samples, 79 tests successful; finite numerical tests are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Finch’s natural first-moment width observable is completely blind to obliquity at fixed disk radius and generator length. The proposed exact second-moment law resolves this structural nonidentifiability, determines the unique minimum and sharp unattained maximum, and gives optimal two-sided inverse stability. The contribution is an all-parameter geometric rigidity statement, not merely a normalization check or a single computed special case.
